source_text: Ὁ δὲ κτίσας θεὸς κακὸν οὐκ ἐποίει οὐδὲ ποιεῖ· [ποιεῖ] καλὸν καὶ ἀγαθόν, ἀγαθὸς γὰρ ὁ ποιῶν.
pass_a_gloss: The God who created does not make evil and does not make, He makes good and noble, for the one making is noble

choices.english: for the one making is noble

pass_b_english: The God who created does not make evil, nor has He ever made it; He makes what is good and noble, because the One who makes is noble.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal gloss and Pass B provides a fluent rendering. The distinction between 'does not make evil' (οὐκ ἐποίει κακὸν) and 'nor has He ever made it' (in Pass B) is a valid stylistic expansion of the imperfect/aorist sense in this context, and the causal relation (γὰρ) is preserved.
